games.title: Grand Theft Auto VI
games.note: Set in Leonida and Vice City, following criminal duo Lucia and Jason, built across Rockstar's worldwide studios.

links.took: Switching between multiple protagonists, modern satirical America and heist-driven open-world crime.
links.added: Criminal partners Lucia and Jason across Leonida's cities, highways and wetlands, with denser interiors.

src.t: Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI official site, 2025

links.extra: First mainline entry in the series since Grand Theft Auto V in 2013.

links.took: Rockstar's upgraded RAGE engine, dense wildlife and weather ecosystems, and reactive NPC world simulation.
links.added: Brought that living-world detail into a modern urban state of traffic, crowds and social media.

src.t: Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI official site, 2025

links.extra: Built by Rockstar's combined global studios following Red Dead Redemption 2.

links.took: Vice City's neon Miami-inspired streets, pastel beachfronts and sun-soaked coastal crime setting.
links.added: Brought Vice City forward from 1986 into modern-day Leonida, surrounded by keys, swamps and highways.

src.t: Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI official site, 2025

links.took: Smooth weighted gunplay transitions and character-driven crime drama across Rockstar's shared studio talent.
links.added: Blended grounded third-person shooting and movement into a dual-protagonist open world across Leonida.

src.t: PC Gamer, Rockstar on sharing Max Payne 3 combat across studios, 2013

links.extra: Continues Rockstar Studios' shared animation and combat pipeline established on Max Payne 3.

links.took: Dropping 100 players from the sky onto a shrinking island to scavenge weapons until one survives.
links.added: Instant wall-and-ramp building from Save the World, cartoon visuals and a free-to-play launch built in two months.

src.t: Ed Zobrist (Epic Games), GDC 2018 talk covered by IGN, Mar 2018
Eurogamer, Epic Games citing PUBG when unveiling Fortnite Battle Royale, Sep 2017

links.extra: Epic's Unreal Tournament team built the mode in two months and made it free two weeks before release.

links.took: Hundred-player island drops, shrinking safe zones, Erangel's map and realistic ballistic gunfights.
links.added: Touchscreen auto-pickup, visual sound cues, shorter arcade modes and free-to-play mobile progression.
links.extra: Co-developed by Tencent's LightSpeed & Quantum Studio and PUBG Studios.

links.took: A freely explorable 3D world with story missions, target locking and Nintendo 64 spatial design.
links.added: Moved 3D exploration into a gritty Liberty City of stolen cars, radio stations and mobster errands.

src.t: Dan Houser (Rockstar), New York Times interview via Kotaku, Nov 2012

links.extra: Sam Houser called GTA III 'Zelda meets Goodfellas'; Dan Houser said every 3D game borrows from N64 Zelda and Mario.

links.took: Moving a character and camera intuitively through a playful, open 3D space.
links.added: Applied that 3D camera and movement freedom to an adult crime city of traffic and pedestrians.

src.t: Dan Houser (Rockstar), New York Times interview via Kotaku, Nov 2012

links.extra: Dan Houser stated that anyone making 3D games who claims not to have borrowed from N64 Mario or Zelda is lying.

links.took: Open-ended freedom to roam, trade or take morally grey jobs in whatever order you choose.
links.added: Brought that open sandbox down from space into a living city of stolen cars and police chases.

src.t: Gary Penn (DMA Design), interview, Game Developer (Gamasutra), Jan 2011
Game Informer, Gary Penn on Grand Theft Auto's troubled development, Feb 2011

links.extra: Creative director Gary Penn summed up DMA Design's vision for the game as 'Elite in a city'.

links.took: Darting through maze-like streets scoring points while relentless pursuers hunt you down.
links.added: Turned the maze into top-down city blocks, the dots into pedestrians and the ghosts into police cars.

src.t: David Jones (DMA Design), Develop conference talk via Kotaku, Jul 2009

links.extra: Creator David Jones compared pedestrians and police cars directly to Pac-Man's dots and ghosts.

links.took: A free-roaming world where you commandeer vehicles and choose which faction's jobs to take.
links.added: Set faction errands inside busy 2D cities full of traffic, radio music and police roadblocks.

src.t: Gary Penn (DMA Design), interview, Game Developer (Gamasutra), Jan 2011
Game Informer, Gary Penn on Grand Theft Auto's troubled development, Feb 2011

links.extra: Gary Penn recalled that DMA Design staff had Mercenary, Elite and Syndicate in mind while reshaping Race'n'Chase.

links.took: Overhead city streets populated by everyday pedestrians, cars and police patrols that react to gunfire.
links.added: Shifted from commanding corporate cyborg squads to solo car theft, arcade score multipliers and phone-booth jobs.

src.t: Gary Penn (DMA Design), interview, Game Developer (Gamasutra), Jan 2011
Game Informer, Gary Penn on Grand Theft Auto's troubled development, Feb 2011

links.extra: Named alongside Elite and Mercenary by Gary Penn among the DMA team's open-city touchstones.
